addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` state or plan that logic shared by files, crates or tools lives in one place they all use (a shared module, crate, or the client template from which code is generated), or that existing duplicated logic is moved into such a place? Judge presence of that statement only, not conflict. An item that simply does not copy anything but says nothing about shared logic has not stated it.

criteria.yes: The item says two or more files, crates or tools use one shared implementation (for example 'both tools call the shared client generated from the template', 'move the duplicated parser into the shared module', 'regenerate the client in both tools from the shared template').
criteria.no: The item says nothing about sharing one implementation: it is silent, adds tool-specific code, only mentions the topic, or copies code.
criteria.unclear: The item hints at sharing but it cannot be told whether one shared implementation is used.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan to copy, paste, duplicate, port or vendor logic from one file, crate or tool into another, so the same logic exists in two places? Regenerating code from one shared template is not copying. An item that is silent about copying does not plan it.

criteria.yes: The item plans to copy, paste, duplicate, port or vendor a function, parser or other logic from one file, crate or tool into another.
criteria.no: The item plans no such copy: it is silent, shares one implementation, generates code from one template, or adds logic with no counterpart elsewhere.
criteria.unclear: The item could be read as duplicating logic, but it is ambiguous.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` change source code that `anchor.scope` covers? The covered code is: source in sc-agent crates (crates/sc-agent*, crates/decidr and the other crates/ members), judge-jev, plan-anchor, and the client template both tools use; an item that adds a helper, parser or function, or copies, ports or vendors code from one file, crate or tool into another, is also covered. Mentioning those names or the topic of duplication without changing code does not count.

criteria.yes: The item adds, changes, copies, ports, vendors or regenerates source code in one of the covered crates, tools or the shared template, or adds a helper, parser or function.
criteria.no: The item changes no covered source code: it is documentation, planning text, CI configuration, tracker work, a discussion, or code elsewhere.
criteria.unclear: The item refers to code changes too vaguely to tell whether covered source is changed.

anchor.statement: sc-agent, judge-jev and plan-anchor code must not copy and paste logic between files or tools, so the code base does not grow unnecessarily.
anchor.scope: adds or changes source code in sc-agent crates (crates/sc-agent*, crates/decidr and the other crates/ members), judge-jev, plan-anchor, or the client template both tools use; adds a helper, parser or function that does the same job as one in another file or tool; copies, ports or vendors code from one file, crate or tool into another

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` state or plan that logic shared by files, crates or tools lives in one place they all use (a shared module, crate, or the client template from which code is generated), or that existing duplicated logic is moved into such a place? Judge presence of that statement only, not conflict. An item that simply does not copy anything but says nothing about shared logic has not stated it.

criteria.yes: The item says two or more files, crates or tools use one shared implementation (for example 'both tools call the shared client generated from the template', 'move the duplicated parser into the shared module', 'regenerate the client in both tools from the shared template').
criteria.no: The item says nothing about sharing one implementation: it is silent, adds tool-specific code, only mentions the topic, or copies code.
criteria.unclear: The item hints at sharing but it cannot be told whether one shared implementation is used.

criteria.no: No step, decision or design in the item goes against the requirement; silence counts as no.
criteria.unclear: A step could be read as going against the requirement, but it is ambiguous.
criteria.yes: A step, decision or design in the item goes against the requirement.

contradicted.instructions: The anchor requires that logic is not copied and pasted between files or tools; shared logic lives in one place both use. Does any step, decision or design in `item.text` go against that requirement, such as: copying, pasting, vendoring or duplicating a function or parser from one tool or file into another? An item that is silent about the requirement does not go against it.

relevant.instructions: Decide whether this anchor applies to `item.text`. It applies only when the item will change code in one of these ways: (1) adds or changes source code in an sc-agent crate (crates/sc-agent*, crates/decidr or another crates/ member), in judge-jev, in plan-anchor, or in the client template both tools use; (2) adds a helper, parser or function; (3) copies, ports or vendors code from one file, crate or tool into another. It does not apply to an item whose work is documentation, notes, CI configuration, tracker work or discussion, even when that item names these tools or talks about duplication.

criteria.no: The item will change no code in any listed way; it is docs, notes, CI configuration, tracker work, discussion, or unrelated code.
criteria.unclear: It cannot be told from the item whether it changes code in a listed way.
